sourceIssues.locator: §3, definition of Pfister forms, p.6, in arXiv 2012.01307v2 (27 April 2023, the final author version, SHA-256 f9f26f7d…2c1f); the published Annals text (198 (2023), 1203–1227) was not collated
sourceIssues.printed: "For an field F and a ∈ F^× set ⟨⟨a⟩⟩ = x_1² − a x_2², respectively ⟨⟨a]] := x_1² + x_1x_2 + a x_2². … If char(F) = 2, then q_a := q_{a_i,…,a_0} := ⟨⟨a_i⟩⟩ ⊗ … ⟨⟨a_1⟩⟩ ⊗ ⟨⟨a_0]]."
sourceIssues.correction: In characteristic 2 the factors ⟨⟨a_j⟩⟩ (j ≥ 1) are the bilinear Pfister forms ⟨1, −a_j⟩_b of [EKM, 9.B], and q_a is their product with the quadratic form ⟨⟨a_0]]: a nonsingular quadratic form of dimension 2^{i+1}.
sourceIssues.reason: With ⟨⟨a⟩⟩ read as the quadratic form x_1² − a x_2² just defined, the tensor product in characteristic 2 is not defined (quadratic forms do not multiply there), and that form is totally singular, being (x_1 + √a x_2)². The reference [EKM, 9.B] has the bilinear factors. Noted by the extraction (item pfister-two).

Re-review by a different agent is needed. Checked at p.6 of arXiv 2012.01307v2 (SHA-256 f9f26f7d…2c1f, the version named): ⟨⟨a⟩⟩ is defined as the quadratic form x₁² − a x₂², and in characteristic 2 the display tensors these quadratic forms with ⟨⟨a₀]]. Quadratic forms have no tensor product in characteristic 2, and x₁² + a x₂² is the square of a linear form over F(√a), hence totally singular. [EKM, 9.B], which the paper cites, builds the quadratic Pfister form as a bilinear Pfister form ⟨⟨a_i,…,a_1⟩⟩_b acting on ⟨⟨a₀]]. The later use (a nonsingular form in 2^{i+1} variables with smooth projective quadric) needs that reading. The intended meaning is clear, so this is a misprint.

sourceIssues.locator: §5, proof of Proposition 5.1, Case 2 (char K = 0), pp.16–17, and the proof of Lemma 5.3, p.17, in arXiv 2012.01307v2 (27 April 2023, the final author version, SHA-256 f9f26f7d…2c1f); the published Annals text (198 (2023), 1203–1227) was not collated
sourceIssues.printed: W_T is defined on p.16 as "the set of geometric prime divisors w of K such that T ⊂ O_w". Case 2 then introduces the geometric prime e-divisors D^e_{K|κ} (full-rank flags, with residue fields κw finite over κ), sets wv := v ∘ w for w ∈ D^e_{K|κ}, and defines "V_T = { wv | w ∈ W_T, v ∈ P_fin(κw) such that wv(t_i) ⩾ 0 }"; the proof of Lemma 5.3 again takes "w ∈ W_T" with Kw = κ[ζ] a number field.
sourceIssues.correction: In Case 2 and Lemma 5.3, W_T should denote {w ∈ D^e_{K|κ} : T ⊂ O_w}, the full-rank geometric flags containing T, not the rank-one divisors of p.16.
sourceIssues.reason: For a rank-one geometric prime divisor w the residue field κw has transcendence degree e − 1 over κ, so it is not a number field and the finite primes P_fin(κw) used next do not apply; the construction needs the rank-e flags just introduced. The symbol is reused for two different sets. Noted by the extraction (items maximal-geometric-flags, arithmetic-flags).

sourceIssues.printed: "Since ḡ ≠ 0, there is an e-tuple ζ in the algebraic closure of κv such that ḡ(ζ) ≠ 0. Then ζ is an e-tuple of roots of unity of order prime to char(κv), and we identify ζ with its lift in the algebraic closure of κ."
sourceIssues.correction: Choose ζ in the torus, with all coordinates nonzero and ḡ(ζ) ≠ 0 (possible because ḡ is a nonzero polynomial over the infinite field κv^alg); then each coordinate is a root of unity of order prime to char(κv) and has a Teichmüller-type lift.
sourceIssues.reason: An element of the algebraic closure of a finite field is a root of unity only if it is nonzero, and a nonvanishing point of ḡ may have zero coordinates. Noted by the extraction (report, §5).

Checked at p.17: the proof picks ζ over the algebraic closure of κv with ḡ(ζ) ≠ 0 and calls it an e-tuple of roots of unity, which fails if a coordinate is 0. The coordinates must also be nonzero for w_{v′}(t_i) ⩾ 0 to hold with t_i ↦ ζ_i a unit and for the Teichmüller lift. The correction is right: T₁⋯T_e·ḡ is a nonzero polynomial over an infinite field, so a torus point with ḡ(ζ) ≠ 0 exists. This is a gap with an immediate repair, and it affects nothing.

sourceIssues.printed: "Since k₁ is relatively algebraically closed in K and k₁v is separable over k₁, K ⊗_{k₁} k₁v is a domain, hence K_v̂ := K k₁v̂ := Quot(K ⊗_{k₁} k₁v) is a well-defined field."
sourceIssues.correction: K_v̂ := K k₁v̂ := Quot(K ⊗_{k₁} k₁v̂), the compositum with the completion. The tensor product is again a domain: K ⊗_{k₁} k₁v̂ = (K ⊗_{k₁} k₁v) ⊗_{k₁v} k₁v̂, where K ⊗_{k₁} k₁v = K k₁v is a field and k₁v̂ is regular over the relatively algebraically closed k₁v.
sourceIssues.reason: The printed definition makes K_v̂ equal to K_v = K k₁v, yet the next sentence treats K_v ⊂ K_v̂ as a proper compositum inside it, and the paper matches K_v̂ with Jannsen's completions F_v. With the hat restored the definition agrees with Jannsen [Ja], Theorem 0.4, which Fact 2.1 quotes.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Proposition 3.2, 3), Case 2, proof of the Claim, p.7, in arXiv 2012.01307v2 (27 April 2023, the final author version, SHA-256 f9f26f7d…2c1f); the published Annals text (198 (2023), 1203–1227) was not collated
sourceIssues.printed: "First, if v′ ∈ P(k′) is not a real place, then E′_{v′} has no orderings; hence by the well-known behaviour of cohomological dimension in field extensions we have cd(E′_{v′}) ⩽ cd(E′) ⩽ dim(E′) + 1 ⩽ dim(Fw) + 1 < r + 1."
sourceIssues.correction: Bound E′_{v′} directly: cd₂(E′_{v′}) ⩽ cd₂(k′_{v′}) + td(E′_{v′} | k′_{v′}) ⩽ 2 + (dim(E′) − 1) = dim(E′) + 1, using cd₂(k′_{v′}) ⩽ 2 for a non-real place (a henselian p-adic or algebraically closed field) and Serre's bound cd(K) ⩽ cd(k) + td(K|k). The rest of the chain is unchanged.
sourceIssues.reason: The middle inequality cd(E′) ⩽ dim(E′) + 1 is false when E′ is formally real, since a field with an ordering has infinite 2-cohomological dimension. That case occurs here: E′ ⊂ E, a field of representatives for Fw, and k′ may have real places, which is why the second half of the proof treats them. The absence of orderings in E′_{v′}, which the sentence invokes, is exactly what makes the direct bound work.
